[1/3] Plan: add trace_navgrid to the editor API, walking a fresh NavAgent from start to goal under a frame budget and reporting found/reached/steps plus the final body state, closing the bake-inspect-route-walk authoring chain

impact_assessment.why: A legal route is not a traversal; an AI could not verify that a controller-driven agent actually reaches a goal through the JSON surface.
impact_assessment.benefits: One action proves walkability with the real agent stack, without mutating the scene or leaving state behind.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: one editor action, editor field and schema entries; dependency: web server imports nav_agent, character and physics; concurrency: session lock; state: ephemeral trace only.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate all numbers and cells, cap the frame budget, use a safe floor height, report unreachable without stepping, pin success and failure traces, and keep the canonical frame unchanged.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Implemented and verified - trace_navgrid parses a schema-1 grid, integer start/goal cells, finite cell_size/origin/height/speed/dt and a bounded frame budget, builds a fresh CharacterBody at the start cell centre, walks a NavAgent over a floor AABB, and reports found, steps, reached and the final nav_agent_report; unreachable goals report found false with zero steps; registered in EDITOR_ACTIONS with schema example and fields, exposed as navgrid_trace, and documented in README/ARCHITECTURE/CHANGELOG and ADR-251; the 5x3 wall trace reaches x > 4.2 grounded while the walled column does not, and six malformed payloads return 400; 1294 tests green, ruff clean, aikit check keystone 6/6 gates, canonical hash 772cac5232a0947b8f6d1914a5cf0cde and 4899-byte reference PNG unchanged; checklists: passed
Task 'keystone-editor-navgride-trace-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: add textured HUD images (Canvas.image with clipping, UV subrects, tint and alpha; a cached clamp-to-edge textured pass in UiRenderer after primitives) with a discovery flag and unchanged default frames

impact_assessment.why: The HUD could draw quads, text and paragraphs but no images, so icons, portraits and textures were impossible without leaving the canvas.
impact_assessment.benefits: Games and AI can render clipped, tinted, subrect HUD images with deterministic edge sampling, and image-only canvases work.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: canvas element type, renderer program/VAO/texture cache and a capability; dependency: canvas imports texture, UiRenderer imports GpuTexture; concurrency: UI renderer state is caller-owned; state: no schema change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate texture/geometry/color/UVs, clip and adjust UVs, use a separate clamp-to-edge cache so 3D wrap policy is untouched, pin orientation/subrects/order/alpha with pixel tests, and keep the canonical frame unchanged.

[1/3] Plan: add root-motion extraction (RootMotion, extract_root_motion, in_place_pose, root_motion_report) that returns a clip root's position/rotation delta, optional planar mode, yaw and a pose copy with the root reset, plus a discovery flag

impact_assessment.why: Clips animate root nodes but the engine had no first-class way to turn that into movement; games had to sample, subtract and invert themselves, and Unity/Unreal expose root motion directly.
impact_assessment.benefits: Animation-driven movement and turning become a pure tested delta, with in-place baking for gameplay and a JSON report for evidence.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new module, four exports and a capability; dependency: root_motion imports animation and scene.Transform; concurrency: none; state: pure values.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate node IDs and times, normalize rotations, pin deltas/yaw/planar/identity/validation with tests, and keep the canonical frame unchanged.

[1/3] Plan: add RootMotionPlayer that advances one clip and returns its pose plus the consumed root delta, composing loop seams and whole cycles, clamping non-loop playback, supporting planar mode and reporting state

impact_assessment.why: Root-motion extraction existed but was inert; a game still had to own a clip clock and compose deltas across loop seams.
impact_assessment.benefits: A walk or turn cycle produces continuous motion across wraps without touching the blending controller, and the pose can be stripped in place for presentation.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new class, one export and a capability; dependency: root_motion only; concurrency: player state is caller-owned; state: no schema change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate clip, node, speed, loop and planar, cap loop spans, pin per-step deltas, wraps, multi-wrap, rotation, clamping, reset and validation, and keep the canonical frame unchanged.

[1/3] Plan: add RootMotionBody that spends a clip's root delta through CharacterController, accumulates yaw, returns an in-place pose and reports state, with planar defaults and a discovery flag

impact_assessment.why: RootMotionPlayer produced deltas but a game still divided by dt, fed a controller, accumulated yaw and stripped the root itself; Unity/Unreal do this for you.
impact_assessment.benefits: Clip-driven movement and turning become one step call with collision, an in-place pose for presentation and a JSON report.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new module, two exports and a capability; dependency: root_motion_body imports root_motion, character and physics; concurrency: rig state is caller-owned; state: no schema change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate types, node, dt and colliders, keep planar the default, pin translation, loops, yaw, walls, completion, reset and reports, and keep the canonical frame unchanged.
